chunks.title: Unit Hook: The Sounding Rocket
chunks.description: Introduce the anchoring phenomenon for Unit 2: the multi-stage launch and trajectory of a suborbital sounding rocket. Show a short, engaging video of a launch. Pose the overarching question: 'How can we describe motion quantitatively?'
resources: Video of a sounding rocket launch

chunks.title: Hexagon Lab 2.1 - Part 1: Initial Data Dive
chunks.description: Students access 'Hexagon Lab - Analyzing Rocket Ascent Data'. They will review the introduction, abstract, and dataset (velocity-time graph) to get familiar with the core data for the unit.

chunks.title: Hexagon Lab 2.1 - Part 2: Graph Analysis
chunks.description: Students begin the investigation portion of the lab, focusing on identifying key features of the v-t graph: initial launch, engine burnout, and apogee. They answer the first set of guiding questions in their notebooks.

chunks.title: Initial Observations & Questions
chunks.description: Groups share their initial findings from the graph. Facilitate a discussion to surface questions and initial hypotheses about the rocket's motion at different stages.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Forecast Introduction
chunks.description: Introduce the 'Research Brief: Telling the complete story of a rocket's journey'. Students read the 'Forecast' prompt and begin brainstorming how they could use the v-t graph to tell a narrative and make a prediction.

chunks.title: Flexbook: Position, Displacement, Velocity
chunks.description: Students engage with the Flexbook reading covering the foundational concepts of motion: Position, Displacement, Distance, Velocity, and Speed. Cornell notes format is encouraged.

chunks.title: Lecture 2.1: The Language of Motion
chunks.description: Mini-lecture clarifying the distinction between scalar (distance, speed) and vector (displacement, velocity) quantities. Emphasize the importance of direction.

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.1 - Part A
chunks.description: Students begin working on the 'Foundational Skills' section of Problem Set 2.1, which focuses on definitions and interpreting motion graphs.

chunks.title: Lecture 2.1: Graphical Analysis
chunks.description: Mini-lecture focusing on interpreting the meaning of the slope of a position-time graph (velocity) and the slope of a velocity-time graph (acceleration).

chunks.title: Hexagon Lab 2.1 - Part 3: Calculating Acceleration
chunks.description: Students return to the rocket ascent data. They now apply their knowledge to calculate the acceleration of the rocket during engine burn and after engine cutoff by finding the slope of the v-t graph.

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.1 - Part B & C
chunks.description: Students work on the 'Application & Synthesis' and 'Reflection' portions of Problem Set 2.1, applying graphical analysis skills to new scenarios.

chunks.title: Problem Set Workshop
chunks.description: Students collaborate in small groups to review their answers for PS 2.1, discuss challenges, and refine their solutions before submission.

chunks.title: Lecture 2.1: Area Under the Curve
chunks.description: Mini-lecture explaining that the area under a velocity-time graph represents displacement. Work through a simple example.

chunks.title: Hexagon Lab 2.1 - Part 4: Calculating Displacement
chunks.description: Students calculate the rocket's height at engine burnout by finding the area under the v-t graph. This provides a key piece of data for their Research Brief.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Forecast Completion
chunks.description: Students finalize their 'Forecast' for the Research Brief, writing a complete narrative of the rocket's journey up to apogee, supported by calculations from the lab.

chunks.title: Forecast Phase Check-in
chunks.description: Brief check-for-understanding quiz on concepts of displacement, velocity, acceleration, and graphical analysis.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Blueprint Introduction
chunks.description: Introduce the 'Blueprint' phase of the research brief, where students will construct the corresponding a-t and p-t graphs to complete their model of the rocket's motion.

chunks.title: Lecture 2.2: The Rules of Falling
chunks.description: Mini-lecture introducing the concept of constant acceleration and deriving the first two kinematic equations.

chunks.title: Flexbook: Kinematics (Constant Acceleration)
chunks.description: Students read the Flexbook section on the kinematic equations, focusing on the conditions under which they apply.

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.2 - Part A (Intro)
chunks.description: Students begin the foundational problems in PS 2.2, practicing the use of the first two kinematic equations.

chunks.title: Lecture 2.2: More Kinematic Equations
chunks.description: Derive and explain the remaining kinematic equations, highlighting the 'timeless' equation ($v_1^2 = v_0^2 + 2ad$).

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.2 - Part A (Continued)
chunks.description: Students continue to work through the foundational problems in PS 2.2, now applying all the kinematic equations.

chunks.title: Whiteboard Kinematics
chunks.description: Assign one challenging problem from PS 2.2 to each group. Groups solve the problem on a whiteboard, showing all steps. They will prepare to present their solution.

chunks.title: Solution Presentations
chunks.description: Each group presents their whiteboard solution to the class. This serves as a review and allows for clarification of common mistakes.

chunks.title: Lecture 2.2: Freefall
chunks.description: Introduce freefall as a special case of constant acceleration where a = -9.80 m/s². Discuss sign conventions and the meaning of 'g'.

chunks.title: Hexagon Lab 2.2 - Freefall Simulations
chunks.description: Students engage with the 'Feather & Bowling Ball' simulation. They perform the investigation with air resistance on and off to conclude that mass does not affect the acceleration of gravity in a vacuum.

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.2 - Freefall Problems
chunks.description: Students work specifically on the freefall problems within PS 2.2, applying the kinematic equations with a = -9.80 m/s².

chunks.title: Revisiting the Rocket
chunks.description: Students apply kinematics to the rocket phenomenon. Using the velocity at engine burnout, they calculate the additional height the rocket gains during its freefall coast to apogee.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Constructing a-t Graph
chunks.description: Using their calculated accelerations from the v-t graph, students construct the acceleration-time graph for the rocket's journey as part of their Blueprint.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Constructing p-t Graph
chunks.description: Students begin constructing the position-time graph. This is the most challenging part, as they need to represent changes in slope (velocity) correctly, showing the parabolic curve during freefall.

chunks.title: Graphing Workshop
chunks.description: Students work in groups, checking each other's p-t graphs. The instructor circulates to address common misconceptions about representing acceleration on a position graph.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Blueprint Finalization
chunks.description: Students finalize their three motion graphs (p-t, v-t, a-t) for the rocket, ensuring they are consistent and tell a coherent story. This completes the Blueprint.

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.2 - Part B & C
chunks.description: Students complete the 'Application & Synthesis' and 'Reflection' portions of PS 2.2, which involve more complex, multi-step kinematics problems.

chunks.title: Problem Set 2.2 Q&A
chunks.description: Dedicated time for students to ask questions about the most challenging problems in PS 2.2. The instructor can work through one or two examples based on student requests.

chunks.title: Consolidation Day
chunks.description: Flexible time for students to complete any outstanding work from the Blueprint phase, review their notes, or ask for individual help.

chunks.title: Consolidation Day
chunks.description: Flexible time for students to complete any outstanding work from the Blueprint phase, review their notes, or ask for individual help.

chunks.title: Modeling a More Complex Reality
chunks.description: Introduce the Reflection phase by posing a question: 'Our model assumes no air resistance, but is that realistic for a rocket?' This sets the stage for the final lab.

chunks.title: Hexagon Lab 2.3 - Modeling Air Resistance
chunks.description: Students engage with the simulation that compares a projectile's trajectory with and without air resistance. They perform the investigation, making qualitative observations.

chunks.title: Discussion: The Effect of Air Resistance
chunks.description: Class discussion based on the lab. How does air resistance affect range and maximum height? How would it change the shape of our rocket's v-t graph?

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Reflection Introduction
chunks.description: Students read the 'Reflection' prompt. They must now write a full narrative of the rocket's flight, supported by their graphs and calculations, and also discuss the limitations of their model (e.g., ignoring air resistance).

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Reflection Writing
chunks.description: Dedicated work time for students to write their final reflection for the research brief, synthesizing all their work from the unit.

chunks.title: Research Brief 2: Peer Review
chunks.description: Students partner up to peer review their research brief reflections, providing feedback on the clarity of the narrative, the accuracy of the evidence, and the thoughtfulness of the model limitations.

chunks.title: Finalizing Unit Work
chunks.description: Final opportunity for students to revise their research briefs based on feedback and ensure all labs and problem sets for the unit are complete.

chunks.title: Unit 2 Review Session
chunks.description: Student-led review session. Students can ask any remaining questions about the major concepts of the unit in preparation for the assessment.

chunks.title: Unit 2 Summative Assessment - Part 1
chunks.description: Students complete the individual, written part of the Unit 2 assessment, covering conceptual questions and quantitative problems.

chunks.title: Unit 2 Summative Assessment - Part 1
chunks.description: Continued work on the summative assessment.

chunks.title: Unit 2 Summative Assessment - Part 2
chunks.description: Students may work on a performance-based or transfer task portion of the assessment, possibly involving a new set of motion data to analyze.

chunks.title: Unit 2 Summative Assessment - Part 2
chunks.description: Continued work on the summative assessment.

chunks.title: Assessment Overflow or Extension Activity
chunks.description: Flexible time for students who need more time on the assessment. For those finished, provide an extension activity, such as analyzing real-world motion data or exploring 2D motion previews.

chunks.title: Assessment Overflow or Extension Activity
chunks.description: Flexible time for students who need more time on the assessment. For those finished, provide an extension activity, such as analyzing real-world motion data or exploring 2D motion previews.

chunks.title: Introduction to Unit 3
chunks.description: Briefly introduce the anchoring phenomenon for Unit 3, 'The Siege at Constantinople', to spark curiosity for the next unit on two-dimensional motion.

chunks.title: Test Corrections & Reflections
chunks.description: If assessments are graded, students can begin test corrections or reflect on their performance and understanding of the unit's major concepts.

chunks.title: Buffer Day
chunks.description: Flexible day to account for unforeseen delays, assemblies, or to dive deeper into a topic of student interest related to kinematics.
